title: U.S. House · Kentucky's 4th District
area: Northern Kentucky, across the Ohio River from Cincinnati, including Covington, Florence and Ashland.

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Thomas Massie (R) lost the May 19, 2026 Republican primary to Ed Gallrein.

candidates.name: Melissa Strange
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 72.4% of the vote, defeating Jesse Brewer.

summary.text: Melissa Strange is the Democratic nominee for Kentucky's 4th Congressional District and is a first-time candidate. A Northern Kentucky native, she has worked as a supply chain director in the agribusiness industry. She campaigns on restoring trust in government, affordability, and protecting individual medical decision-making, including abortion access.

background.text: Born and raised in Villa Hills, Kentucky, and now lives in Erlanger, according to her campaign website as reported by WCPO.
A graduate of Dixie Heights High School, Northern Kentucky University and Thomas More University, according to LINK nky.

Has worked for nearly 30 years as a supply chain director for a global nutrition and agribusiness company; LINK nky reports she is a director of supply chain management at Archer Daniels Midland in Erlanger.
Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 72.4% of the vote, defeating Jesse Brewer, to become the nominee for the open seat.
LINK nky reports she lives in Erlanger with her husband and has two sons.

priorities.text: "RESTORE FAITH AND TRUST IN GOVERNMENT ... Elected officials must conduct themselves with honesty, integrity, and transparency, demonstrating a clear commitment to public service, NOT to personal enrichment."

"AFFORDABLE AND ACCESSIBLE QUALITY OF LIFE ... All citizens should be able to afford basic needs such as food, clothing, shelter, healthcare, and education, and everyone deserves to be paid a fair, livable wage."

positions.summary: Supports protecting the right to personal medical decisions, including reproductive care, from government interference at the federal level.
positions.quote: The right of an individual to make personal medical decisions without government interference is also fundamental. We all have the right to decide what is best for each of us and for our own bodies. Private health decisions should be made between patients and medical professionals, not by legislators.

positions.summary: Says all citizens should be able to afford basic needs including healthcare, as part of a platform of affordable, accessible quality of life.
Says everyone deserves to be paid a fair, livable wage.

candidates.name: Ed Gallrein
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated incumbent Thomas Massie in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary.

summary.text: Ed Gallrein is the Republican nominee for Kentucky's 4th Congressional District. A retired Navy SEAL officer and fifth-generation farmer, he ran for the state Senate in 2024 and lost the primary, then won the 2026 Republican primary against incumbent Thomas Massie with President Trump's endorsement. His campaign website lists cutting taxes and regulation, border security, gun rights, and opposition to abortion as priorities.

background.text: Born in 1958; his campaign website says he was born and raised in Kentucky and is a fifth-generation farmer whose family has worked the land for over a century.

Earned a bachelor's degree in agriculture from Murray State University in 1981 and a master's degree in agribusiness economics in 1984, according to Wikipedia. It also lists master's degrees from the Naval Postgraduate School and the Air War College.

Served in the U.S. Navy from 1984 to 2014 as a SEAL officer, rising to the rank of Captain, according to his campaign website and Wikipedia. His campaign says he served on seven SEAL teams or units, including SEAL Team Six, and deployed from Panama to the Persian Gulf.
His campaign website lists three Bronze Star Medals and two Presidential Unit Citations among his military awards.

After leaving the Navy he returned to Kentucky as a farmer and business owner, according to his campaign website; Wikipedia states he has operated Circle G Farm and Stables in Shelby County since 2014.
Ran in the May 2024 Republican primary for Kentucky State Senate District 7 and finished second, receiving 38.3% to Aaron Reed's 39.3%. Before the 2026 race he had never held elective office.
Entered the 2026 race in October 2025 after President Trump endorsed him, and defeated incumbent Thomas Massie in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary, 54.9% to 45.1%.

priorities.text: On the economy, Gallrein said he would work to "cut taxes, stop the reckless spending that has driven up inflation, and fight to bring good-paying jobs back home to Kentucky."

positions.summary: Campaigns on cutting taxes and reducing federal spending.
positions.quote: cut taxes, stop the reckless spending that has driven up inflation, and fight to bring good-paying jobs back home to Kentucky.

positions.summary: Says he would work with President Trump to finish the border wall and fully fund Border Patrol and ICE.
positions.quote: team up with President Trump to finish the wall, fully fund Border Patrol & ICE, and finally secure the border once and for all.

positions.summary: Says he will protect the right to keep and bear arms without compromise.
positions.quote: as a lifelong defender of freedom and warrior for our Nation, Gallrein will protect our right to keep and bear arms without compromise.

summary.text: Jeremy Todd is the Libertarian Party nominee for Kentucky's 4th Congressional District. In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he describes himself as a Christian and a Libertarian with a business career. He campaigns on reducing federal debt and money printing, ending overseas military commitments, and opposing government surveillance.

background.text: In his Ballotpedia survey, he says he was born and raised in the South, the son of a truck driver and a billing clerk.
He says he built a career in business, leading teams ranging from a handful of employees to organizations of more than 300 people. The survey does not name employers.
He describes himself as a husband and father who holds Christian and Libertarian views, favoring individual liberty, limited government and personal responsibility.

priorities.text: "As a Christian and a Libertarian, he believes in individual liberty, personal responsibility, limited government, and protecting the freedoms guaranteed to every American."

positions.summary: Supports closing overseas U.S. military bases and reducing foreign military commitments generally.
positions.quote: If you elect me, I will advocate to close our overseas bases, bring our brave troops back home to their loved ones, and focus our resources on defending our own homeland.

summary.text: Peter Harmon Williams is an independent write-in candidate for Kentucky's 4th Congressional District. No campaign website, public statements, or biographical profile were found for this candidate.
